[LCYC.2.3.2] There is no sensible runtime behaviour to fall
back on. Such a rule set could oscillate, settle
on one answer depending on which rule the engine
evaluated first, or behave differently across
platforms — the author has written something
without a clear meaning. That is why [LCYC.3.4]
gives this shape its own diagnostic rather than
the generic cycle error: the failure is an
underspecified rule set, not merely a loop.

idris.name: lcyc_2_3_2__defeat_halts
idris.note: Executed and checked: the pair halts after exactly one firing, the first rule in source order wins, the other never fires -- the clause's "settle on one answer depending on which rule the engine evaluated first", with the rule fixed by [LDET.5.4]. Over explicit facts; see `lcyc_2_3_1__defeat_prog`.
